'''Shih-Jen Hwang''' (born 1960)<ref name=":1" /> is a Taiwanese-American biostatistician and epidemiologist. She is a staff scientist in the Laboratory for Cardiovascular Epidemiology and Genomics at the [[National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Laboratory of Cardiovascular Epidemiology and Genomics |url=https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/science/cardiovascular-epidemiology-and-genomics |access-date=2022-08-26 |website=[[National Institutes of Health]]}}</ref> She is an investigator on the [[Framingham Heart Study]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Shih-Jen Hwang |url=https://profiles.bu.edu/ShihJen.Hwang |access-date=2022-08-27 |website=[[Boston University]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==

Hwang completed a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in nursing at [[Kaohsiung Medical University]] and an [[M. P. H.|M.P.H.]] in epidemiology at the [[National Taiwan University]]. She then earned an [[Master of Health Science|M.H.S.]] and [[Ph.D.]] in epidemiology at [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health]].<ref name=":0" /> Her 1994 doctoral dissertation was titled, ''Study of oral clefts: search for genetic variability and gene-environment interaction''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis |last=Hwang |first=Shih-Jen |date=1994 |title=Study of oral clefts: search for genetic variability and gene-environment interaction |journal= |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=[[Johns Hopkins University]] |oclc=39064898}}</ref>
